messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prefix-cache miss-rate spike detected for tier=prod, affected services: api-layer, route=/v1/generate. Auto-escalation -> paging liam (oncall). severity=P1 :rotating_light:
liam: saw it. I'm on it. pinging @jess and @maria for cache/runtime context. what's the downstream error rate?
jess: 502s up ~3x from baseline in the last 2m. frontend errors spiking. tracing shows longer tails on first token.
maria: oncall note: recent cache-control change rolled 2h ago (eviction-ttl reduced from 30m -> 5m) for experiment RED-204. Could be related.
sam: confirming metrics: prefix_hit_rate dropped from 98% -> 64% across 3 regions (us-west/us-east/eu). KV miss traffic increased 6x.
liam: impact? customer-facing? any billing/requests dropped?
jess: note from product-monitoring: ~12% of production requests got degraded fallthrough to smaller model (fallback path) due to miss flood. Several customers reported latency timeouts.
maria: grabbing logs for the time window. running quick query:
```
# logql-style
{service="runtime",env="prod"} | json | prefix like "user_prefix_" | rate(5m)
```
maria: top lines show rapid cache eviction events around 1936000900-1936001100. sample: 
```
[1936000958] EVICT prefix=user_prefix_abc shard=12 cause=ttl_expire ttl=300 evicted_keys=42
[1936000981] EVICT prefix=user_prefix_xyz shard=8 cause=ttl_expire ttl=300 evicted_keys=31
```
liam: Those ttl values look like 300s (5m) — matches RED-204. Who promoted that change?
maria: rollout was rolled by tom at 1915 UTC, 4% canary then 100% after metrics looked ok. commit: a1b2c3d (config/cache/ttl).
tom: ack, that was me. We saw no regressions in canary but load patterns might have differed.
sam: hypothesis A: aggressive TTL caused mass rewarm leading to KV cache contention/paging; spills increased latencies and then cascade into more misses.
jess: hypothesis B: rewarm controller has a bug under burst when many prefixes must be re-cached, resulting in throttled background rewarm -> sustained miss rate. logs show rewarm-worker errors: 
```
[1936001002] ERROR rewarm-worker timeout rewarm for prefix=user_prefix_foo retries=3
```
liam: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback TTL to 30m, 2) temporarily increase rewarm concurrency, 3) enable emergency sticky-cache (pin hot prefixes). Which is fastest?
maria: fastest is to revert the config -> rollback to previous TTL. I can prep rollback and push with tom's signoff. Rolling back should restore hit-rate within a couple minutes as TTLs stop expiring.
tom: I approve rollback. I'll trigger canary rollback to 10% then 100% if green.
jess: while rollback is happening, can we scale up KV nodes by +25% and bump rewarm-worker concurrency? Sam, can you run scale?
sam: scaling KV pool now (k8s job -> scale statefulset replicas +2). rewarm concurrency increase applied to rewarm-controller (configmap update).
incident-bot: ACTION: rollback started by tom at 1936001250. status=canary(10%).
liam: moving customer-facing comms: notifying support to stitch incidents to affected customers. any expected downtime?
jess: no downtime, but temporary higher latencies until hit-rate recovers. support-template drafted.
maria: sharing quick dashboard links: https://dash.internal/redwood/prefix-cache?from=1936000800&to=1936001400
liam: handoff note: I'm going to be out for an urgent call in ~15m. Jess, can you take primary and update this thread?
jess: taking over. liam, thx.
incident-bot: UPDATE: rollback progress -> canary 10% healthy. KV scale job succeeded, rewarm concurrency increased.
sam: KV pool replicas: before=8 after=10. rewarm-controller concurrency: before=5 after=20.
maria: observing hit_rate -> improved from 64% -> 81% within 2m of concurrency bump, and ~92% after rollback to previous TTL was applied cluster-wide at 1936001320.
jess: good. continue to monitor for 30m. we should collect timeline for RCA. I'll assemble initial timeline and we can add logs below.
liam: quick timeline (rough):
- 1936000900: TTL change rolled (RED-204) completed
- 1936000958: first eviction bursts detected
- 1936001000: KV miss rate begins to climb sharply
- 1936001122: ALERT auto-escalation and paging
- 1936001200: mitigation actions (scale KV, bump rewarm concurrency)
- 1936001250: rollback to TTL=30m canary started
- 1936001320: cluster-wide TTL rollback completed; hit-rate recovering

jess: saving those. Maria, can you paste the raw rewarm-worker stack traces we saw? We'll attach to RCA.
maria: pasting snippet: 
```
[1936001002] ERROR rewarm-worker timeout rewarm prefix=user_prefix_foo stack=worker.go:142, rewarm.go:88, http.go:44
[1936001010] WARN rewarm-queue backlog=512 inflight=7
```
sam: also observed increased disk I/O on KV nodes around the same timeframe (iops spiked 4x).
liam: action items for follow-up (RCA):
- Verify canary testing gap for RED-204 (traffic profile mismatch) -> owner: tom
- Add safety limit to TTL changes that simulate burst scenarios -> owner: eng-runtime (maria)
- Improve rewarm-controller backpressure handling and observability -> owner: eng-runtime (maria)
- Run load replay for TTL=5m to confirm steady-state -> owner: SRE (sam)
- Postmortem draft and customer impact summary -> owner: jess

jess: I'm going to tag this incident as P1->Resolved (mitigated). moving to postmortem channel thread after 30m stable. If anyone sees a relapse ping me. :white_check_mark:
liam: quick handoff note for oncall rotation: root cause hypothesis currently: TTL reduction caused mass evictions -> rewarm/backfill couldn't cope -> KV paging and increased latency -> cascade into misses and fallbacks. Pending deeper log correlation.
tom: will open PR to add canary traffic-slice tests.
maria: will add metrics to alert on rewarm-queue backlog and worker timeouts.
sam: will run replay and attach artifacts to postmortem.
jess: thanks team. closing active response. Next update in postmortem thread with timeline and logs.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: mitigation succeeded, status=resolved at 1936002350.
